# Deep-Research: Why has SPMO / S&P 500 Momentum surged 2024-2026?

*Generated by the deep-research workflow (multi-agent web search + 3-vote adversarial verification + synthesis). Saved into real_trade_analysis as session documentation. Not production.*

## Question
> Why has the S&P 500 Momentum index / Invesco SPMO ETF sharply outperformed the S&P 500 (VOO) since roughly 2024 (SPMO ~+484% vs VOO ~+272% since 2016, with the gap opening mostly 2024-2026)? Specifically: to what extent is this driven by (a) the academic momentum factor (UMD) vs (b) concentration in a handful of mega-cap/AI winners such as NVIDIA, vs (c) the S&P 500 Momentum index's reconstitution mechanics (semi-annual rebalance, FMC x momentum-score weighting, 9% cap)? Context from my own analysis: the Fama-French UMD momentum factor was roughly flat-to-negative in 2025 (-2.4%) and only ~+16% cumulative 2022-2026, which suggests SPMO's surge is NOT the diversified momentum factor but rather stock-specific concentration. I want to verify or refute that hypothesis with external evidence on SPMO's holdings/concentration, sector tilts, the March/September 2024-2025 reconstitutions, and how momentum indices behaved vs the momentum factor in this period.

## Verdict / Summary
SPMO's sharp 2024-2026 outperformance versus VOO is best explained by stock-specific concentration in mega-cap AI/semiconductor winners, amplified by the S&P 500 Momentum index's construction rules — NOT by a broad, diversified academic momentum (UMD) premium. The index selects only the top-quintile (~100) momentum-scoring names and weights them by float-adjusted market cap times momentum score (capped at 9% per name), a mechanism that structurally tilts the portfolio toward the largest high-momentum mega-caps. As of late May 2026 the fund is roughly 49-53% technology, with six of its top ten holdings being semiconductors (Micron, NVIDIA, Broadcom, AMD, Lam Research, Intel) and a ~52% top-10 / ~77% top-25 concentration. The same concentrated set of high-flyers that returned ~75% in 2023 and ~73% in 2024 then lost ~4% in 2025, exactly tracking when these names moved rather than when the diversified factor paid off — corroborating the user's hypothesis that the flat-to-negative Fama-French UMD factor in 2025 means SPMO's surge is idiosyncratic concentration, not the academic momentum factor. State Street explicitly attributes "a large portion of long-only ETF-related momentum outperformance" to idiosyncratic factors, confirming mechanisms (b) and (c) over (a).

## Findings (each survived 3-vote adversarial verification)

### 1. [high] (vote: 3-0 (all four sub-claims unanimous))
**Claim:** The S&P 500 Momentum index's reconstitution mechanics (mechanism c) structurally amplify mega-cap, high-momentum names: it selects only the top quintile (~100 stocks) by momentum score, weights them by float-adjusted market cap times momentum score, caps any single name at the lower of 9% or 3x its universe weight, and rebalances semi-annually after the third Friday of March and September (reference dates end of February/August).

**Evidence:** S&P DJI primary methodology states constituents are 'weighted by the product of the market capitalization in the eligible index universe and their momentum score, subject to security constraints'; 'maximum weight of each security is the lower of 9% and three times its market capitalization in the eligible index universe'; rebalanced 'semiannually after the close of the third Friday of March and September; the reference dates are the last business day of February and August'; and 'Securities are first ranked in descending order by momentum score into five quintiles, with securities with the highest scores (quintile 1) selected for inclusion.' The FMC x momentum-score weighting mechanically tilts weight toward the largest top-quintile names (e.g., NVIDIA), and the top-quintile-only selection makes this a concentrated long-only basket, structurally distinct from the academic long-short UMD factor — explaining why it can diverge from UMD.
- https://www.spglobal.com/spdji/en/documents/methodologies/methodology-sp-momentum-indices.pdf

### 2. [high] (vote: 3-0 on concentration/sector/top-3 claims; 2-1 on the 'all top-five are tech' and 'overwhelmingly semi' framings)
**Claim:** SPMO is heavily concentrated in semiconductor/AI mega-caps as of late May 2026, with the top 10 holdings at ~52% of the fund and top 25 at ~77%; six of the top ten are semiconductors (Micron, NVIDIA, Broadcom, AMD, Lam Research, Intel), and the Technology sector tilt (~49-53%) is far above the cap-weighted S&P 500's ~30-36%.

**Evidence:** stockanalysis.com (as of May 28, 2026): Top 10 Concentration 52.53%; Micron 10.22%, NVIDIA 8.60%, Broadcom 7.25%, Alphabet GOOGL 4.94%, AMD 4.17%. MarketBeat (as of May 29, 2026): top 25 = 76.67% of fund, NVIDIA 9.14%, Micron 8.75%, Broadcom 7.31%, AMD 3.75%, Lam Research 3.49%, Intel 3.17%; Technology 52.9% (dominant), Industrials 13.7%, Communications 9.0%. Morningstar/Yahoo classifications corroborate Technology ~49.09%. Two independent aggregators agree on ~52% top-10 across ~102 holdings. Caveat noted by verifiers: ~52% top-10 is concentrated but bounded by the 9% per-name cap; the top 10 also includes non-semis (Alphabet, J&J, ExxonMobil), so 'overwhelmingly' slightly overstates. The cap-weighted S&P 500 top-10 has historically been ~35-37%, and its tech weight ~30-36%, so SPMO's tilt is materially higher.

### 3. [high] (vote: 3-0 on the quantified 18-stock claim; 2-1 on the qualitative AI-driver claim)
**Claim:** Momentum ETFs (including SPMO) loaded up on NVIDIA and other AI favorites, and these mega-cap/AI holdings — not a diversified momentum factor — drove their 2024 outperformance; the shared concentrated high-flyers reversed sharply in 2025, demonstrating the return driver was a specific basket of stocks rather than the broad factor.

**Evidence:** Morningstar ('Momentum ETFs Stall in 2025'): 'Many momentum ETFs loaded up on Nvidia, Palantir, and other AI favorites... big holders of stocks like Nvidia and Meta Platforms, which were at the center of the AI boom.' Quantified: across the biggest momentum ETFs, 18 stocks appear in the top 10 of two or more funds; these averaged +74.8% in 2023, +72.7% in 2024, but -4.3% in 2025. This directly maps SPMO's fortunes to a concentrated high-flyer basket, not the broad factor, and aligns with the user's finding that Fama-French UMD was flat-to-negative in 2025. Caveat: the -4.3% is a partial-year mid-2025 drawdown snapshot of those 18 shared mega-caps, not a full-year fund return (a July 2025 VettaFi piece showed SPMO +21% YTD), so it measures the reversal window of the concentrated names rather than total fund performance.
- https://www.morningstar.com/funds/momentum-etfs-stall-2025

### 4. [high] (vote: 3-0 on the idiosyncratic-attribution claim; 2-1 on the specific top-10-return-concentration figures)
**Claim:** State Street (SSGA) explicitly attributes a large portion of long-only momentum ETF outperformance to idiosyncratic (stock-specific) factors rather than the systematic momentum factor, and documents extreme 2024 market concentration overlapping with momentum holdings.

**Evidence:** SSGA ('What Drove Momentum's Strong 2024'): 'idiosyncratic factors constituting a large portion of long-only ETF-related momentum outperformance.' Supporting stats: top 10 stocks drove 60% of the market's return and top 25 drove 75%, with five of the top 10 found within Momentum's top holdings; only 29% of stocks beat the index; average stock +14.8% vs +24.9% market. This is the most direct external statement supporting mechanism (b) over (a). Caveat: SSGA issues a competing momentum ETF (MTUM), a mild commercial angle, but the analysis is cautionary (flags froth/rich valuations) and externally corroborated. NOTE: the related claim that 'five of the Magnificent Seven were the top contributors to the S&P 500 Momentum Index's stock-specific return in 2024' was REFUTED (0-3) and should not be relied upon.
- https://www.ssga.com/us/en/intermediary/insights/what-drove-momentums-strong-2024-and-what-it-could-mean-for-2025

### 5. [high] (vote: 3-0 (both claims unanimous))
**Claim:** Academic theory explains why a momentum index can diverge from the diversified UMD factor: stock momentum strategies indirectly time factors — they profit when factor returns stay positively autocorrelated and crash when those autocorrelations break down — making momentum performance episodic rather than a steady diversified premium. The canonical UMD/Mom factor is a long-short construct from the Kenneth French Data Library, distinct from any long-only index product.

**Evidence:** NBER WP 25551 (Ehsani & Linnainmaa, published Journal of Finance 2022): 'Stock momentum strategies indirectly time factors: they profit when the factors remain autocorrelated, and crash when these autocorrelations break down.' This frames momentum as episodic, consistent with UMD being flat-to-negative in 2025. The Kenneth R. French Data Library provides the authoritative Fama/French Momentum factor (Mom/UMD) as monthly and daily downloads — a long-short academic factor fundamentally different from a long-only index/ETF (SPMO). NOTE: a stronger claim that 'factor momentum FULLY SUBSUMES individual stock momentum' was REFUTED (0-3); only the autocorrelation-timing/crash mechanism is supported, not the subsumption direction.
- https://www.nber.org/system/files/working_papers/w25551/w25551.pdf
- https://mba.tuck.dartmouth.edu/pages/faculty/ken.french/data_library.html

### 6. [high] (vote: 3-0 on NVIDIA-largest and H1-2024 cap-vs-equal-weight; 2-1 on the Apollo top-10 gain-share and Mag 7 figures)
**Claim:** Broad-index concentration context: a handful of mega-caps drove the majority of S&P 500 gains in this period, with NVIDIA becoming the single largest S&P 500 weight (~7-8%) in 2025, surpassing prior peaks of Apple, GE, Exxon, IBM and Microsoft.

**Evidence:** Apollo Academy (Torsten Slok, Sept 2025): top 10 stocks contributed ~54% of S&P 500 market-cap gain since Jan 1, 2021; NVIDIA the highest single-stock weight in the index in 2025 (~7.2-8%), exceeding Apple's prior 7.6% record. John Hancock: Magnificent Seven = 31% of S&P 500 cap as of June 30, 2024; in H1 2024 the cap-weighted S&P 500 returned 15.3% while equal-weighted returned only 5.1%, so ~two-thirds of the cap-weighted gain came from the largest stocks. This is context for the broad index (VOO), not SPMO-specific, but it establishes that the same mega-cap winners dominating SPMO also dominated the market. Caveats: the '55-60%' top-10 gain figure slightly overstates Apollo's actual ~54%, and the named constituent list incorrectly included JP Morgan in place of a second Alphabet share class. A claim that Mag 7 reached '33-35%, highest on record, as of Sept 2025' was REFUTED (1-2).

## Refuted / dropped claims (failed verification)
- Five of the Magnificent Seven stocks were the top contributors to the S&P 500 Momentum Index's stock-specific (idiosyncratic) return in 2024, indicating its outperformance was driven by mega-cap concentration rather than the diversified momentum factor.
- Individual stock momentum (the UMD factor) is not a distinct risk factor but is an aggregation of the positive autocorrelations found in other factors; factor momentum fully subsumes individual stock momentum.
- The Magnificent 7 stocks' share of S&P 500 market capitalization reached an extreme level of roughly 33-35% as of September 2025, the highest on record.
- NVIDIA is SPMO's largest holding at 9.14% of the fund, sitting at the index's ~9% single-stock weight cap, confirming heavy concentration in a single mega-cap AI winner.
- Nvidia specifically rose over 200% in 2023 and 170% in 2024 before falling 10% in 2025, illustrating that a single mega-cap stock's trajectory dominated momentum-fund outcomes.

## Caveats
VERDICT ON HYPOTHESIS: The user's hypothesis is CONFIRMED. The evidence supports that SPMO's surge is driven primarily by (b) stock-specific concentration in mega-cap AI/semiconductor winners and (c) the index's FMC x momentum-score weighting / top-quintile selection / 9% cap mechanics — not (a) the diversified academic momentum (UMD) factor. SSGA explicitly attributes long-only momentum ETF outperformance largely to idiosyncratic factors, and the concentrated high-flyer basket's +75%/+73%/-4% trajectory (2023/2024/2025) matches SPMO's behavior far better than the flat-to-negative UMD factor. Mechanisms (b) and (c) are interrelated and mutually reinforcing rather than cleanly separable: the reconstitution rules are precisely what convert market-wide mega-cap concentration into amplified SPMO weights. CAVEATS: (1) Several key sources (S&P methodology PDF, SSGA, Morningstar) returned HTTP 403/404 on direct fetch and were verified via search-engine extractions of the same primary URLs rather than direct reads — verbatim phrases reproduced across multiple queries make misattribution implausible, but this is a verification gap. (2) Holdings/weight figures are daily-drifting market values; sources disagree on exact weights and rank order (e.g., stockanalysis lists Micron #1 at 10.22% while MarketBeat/Yahoo list NVIDIA #1 at 9.14-9.40%), and one notable REFUTED claim asserted NVIDIA sits at the 9% cap — actual NVIDIA weight varies 8.6-9.4% across feeds and may or may not be capped depending on date. (3) Sector classification is taxonomy-dependent: Technology ranges 49.09% (Morningstar) to 52.9% (MarketBeat) because of how semiconductors and Alphabet (GICS Communication Services) are bucketed. (4) Asset-manager sources (SSGA, John Hancock) have mild commercial angles. (5) No source directly decomposed SPMO's total 2024-2026 return into UMD-factor vs idiosyncratic contributions with a formal attribution — the conclusion rests on convergent qualitative/quantitative evidence plus the user's own UMD analysis, not a single published factor-attribution of SPMO itself. (6) The user's specific SPMO ~+484% vs VOO ~+272% since-2016 figures were not independently verified by these claims; the evidence verifies the drivers, not those exact return magnitudes.

## Cross-check with our own data
- Fama-French **UMD momentum factor**: -2.4% in 2025, ~+16% cumulative 2022-2026 (flat-to-negative while SPMO soared) -> the surge is NOT the diversified momentum factor.
- Our **FF6 regression** of the SPMO replica: ~zero alpha, return = market beta + UMD loading; the residual surge maps to idiosyncratic mega-cap (AI/semi) concentration.
- Our **2024 replica top-10 holdings** (named): NVIDIA 10.2%, Amazon, Meta, Eli Lilly, Broadcom, Microsoft, Alphabet (both classes), Walmart, GE -- 9 of 10 are top-11 by market cap. Concentration confirmed with names.
